newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FIN MIN MULLS EVEN MORE BUDGET CUTS - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FIN MIN MULLS EVEN MORE BUDGET CUTS - PAPER.

text.p: The Finnish finance ministry is planning new spending cuts to balance the state budget next year if necessary, on top of a criticised plan to reduce the 1998 deficit by four billion markka, daily Helsingin Sanomat reported on Thursday.

It gave no details and did not identify its sources, but said one of the reasons for the plans was an extra seven billion markka increase in state debt this year caused by the dollar's and sterling's advances which may threaten Finland's chances to meet the criteria for joining Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
The paper said the planned cuts would hit all sectors.

The finance ministry has proposed reducing next year's budget deficit to 17 billion markka from an earlier planned 21 billion, but this has sparked objections from many cabinet ministers. Total budget spending would be 188 billion markka.
This year's deficit is projected at around 26 billion markka, down from some 34 billion in 1996.
Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen has expressed support for the austerity plan, and he is expected to spell out his economic policy views at a news conference on Thursday at 1300/1000 GMT.
